data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# PBS resources:
#   -P vp91
#   -q normal
#   -l walltime=00:20:00
#   -l ncpus=16
#   -l mem=64gb
#   -N gw_amr
#   -l wd

#flux: --job-name=gw_amr
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 16
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=20m

# Omitted PBS option: -l mem=64gb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -P vp91 (project/account)
# Flux accounting/project selection is site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may be charged to a default project/account or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted PBS option: -q normal (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or be rejected by policy.

# PBS -l wd changes to the submission directory; under Flux emulate with submit dir.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

source "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}/modules.sh"

# PBS used mpiexec; under Flux, use flux-run to launch ranks.
flux run -n 16 -c 1 julia --project="${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}" -e '
  using GadiTutorial;
  main_amr(;nprocs=16,nrefs=4,num_amr_steps=6)
'

reasons: PBS requested 64GB of memory (`-l mem=64gb`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

PBS specified a queue and project/account (`-q normal`, `-P vp91`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/account selection; on sites where these affect eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

#!/bin/bash
#PBS -P vp91
#PBS -q normal
#PBS -l walltime=00:20:00
#PBS -l ncpus=16
#PBS -l mem=64gb
#PBS -N gw_amr
#PBS -l wd

source $PBS_O_WORKDIR/modules.sh

mpiexec -n 16 julia --project=$PBS_O_WORKDIR -e'
  using GadiTutorial;
  main_amr(;nprocs=16,nrefs=4,num_amr_steps=6)
'
